title: OnUserSignInSuccess is not called for AutoSignin. - Behavior bug?
body:
When **auto sign** is Configured, OnUserSignInSuccess is not called when a login occurs.  

When auto sign in is NOT configured, and UserSignOn is requested directly, OnUserSignInSuccess is properly called.
author: MattB-msft

comments.body: I confirm this behavior
to doc - in Auth docs - will close and add to backlog

This is intentional.  I have been pointing this out for some time and is the behavior from Teams AI SDK.  Auto was designed to continue with the original Activity after sign in is complete.  

What is different from Teams AI SDK is the manual sign in.  There the (equivelent) call to SignInUser would return a token if the user was already signed in.  Otherwise it would later call OnUserSignInSuccess when the multi-turn sign in was complete.

title: `turnState` not persisted across turns
author: rido-min

comments.body:
This is harder to spot because Teams AI SDK would default to "Temp" state if the ITurnState.SetValue did not include the state name.

i.e., `turnState.SetValue("counter")` is the same as `turnState.Temp.SetValue("counter")`.

Where `turnState.SetValue("conversation.counter")` is the same as `turnState.Conversation.SetValue("counter")`.
See my comment about your use of ITurnState.SetValue.  It doesn't matter what your storage is, it's going to Temp state.

sure.. although we cannot assume users will read the comments. We need docs explaining the design.

Are you saying that using a scope the value will be persisted?

If I use `turnState.SetValue("my.counter", counter++);` I got an exception `Error: Scope 'my' not found`, probably because I didnt initialize it properly.

I also tried 

```cs
int counter = turnState.GetValue("conversation.counter", () => 0);
turnState.SetValue("conversation.counter", counter++);
```

with no luck

TurnStateFactory is called at the beginning of the turn.  Which means that if your AgentApplication is (effectively) transient, then you are getting a new MemoryStorage each turn. 

`my` would only be a valid scope if you added an appropriate IAgentState implementation with that name.  See TurnState for an example.  It adds ConversatationState, UserState, etc... or whatever TurnState was constructed with.  In theory, you could add an new `AgentState` implementation named `my`.
I'm not entirely sold on defaulting to `Temp` for a missing scope.  But then... I suppose technically an agent doesn't need state at all.  Though I would bet most do.
It's an interesting experiment to find gaps, but 100% if state wasn't working, neither would other things.  Like User Authorization, or the DotNet EchoBot sample.

I assume you are using either a Controller or the minimal AspNet routes (MapPost)?  In that case, it uses DI to get the IAgent.  Are you adding that to DI as transient?  In which case, create a MemoryStorage outside that.

You shouldn't have to call Load/Save, as the AgentApplication does.  Though it's conceivable there could be a need to call Save manually.  Perhaps.
It's clear there needs to more comments, docstr, etc... around TurnStateFactory in cases where people want to construct via code (as opposed to configuration).

In theory AgentApplication would work as a singleton.  But we haven't really vetted that.  Though AddRoute/Enumerte has locking.  

This is complicated by a recent ask of supporting multiple IAgents in a single host.  But different topic.

But for what you are doing, create MemoryStorage outside the `AddAgent` and make it:

`TurnStateFactory = () => new TurnState(storage)`
Which is to say... Before `OnActivity` is even evaluated, `AgentApplication` calls:  `Options.TurnStateFactory()`.  So in your case... new MemoryStorage each time.

I think most of the behavior discussed in this issue can be simplified by requesting an instance of the IStorage, without any factory, in AgentApplicationOptions.

.. and we can discuss later if makes sense to have AgentApplication as transient.

> I think most of the behavior discussed in this issue can be simplified by requesting an instance of the IStorage, without any factory, in AgentApplicationOptions.

AgentApplication.OnTurnAsync expects a new instance of ITurnState.  Even if AgentApplication was singleton, this would be true.
Its just that with MemoryStorage, IStorage needs to be singleton.

> What are you trying to solve?

I'm trying to understand the detailed design of Application and TurnState to replicate in JS. As we dont have DI I'm trying to minimize  the use of DI as much as possible for easier apple-to-apple comparison.

I'm going with the first option you suggested, even by using a Singleton for MemoryStorage, and TurnState is not persisted across turns, so wondering if I'm doing something wrong or if this is a bug.

Related to this there is another important decision to make IStorage required when using the AgentApplication object, with or without DI.

Probably would need to see a complete repro for this.  This just hasn't been an issue for me in any sample/test-bot, and I guess I'm not seeing what you are doing differently and what changes we could make to minimize this.

title: Feature Request: Create more robustness in configuration
body:
Currently when trying to use libraries like MSAL and other parts of the Agents framework it requires us to setup our appsettings.json a certain way with certain settings.  

One example of where this is done is when calling the "AddDefaultMsalAuth" method where you have to send in a configuration section for "MSALConfiguration".

Most of my enterprise level applications have custom configuration code where we inject various configurations from different locations and variations.  Rather then have the libraries pull directly from configuration could we possibly have an option to send in the variables directly?  I find myself having to write code to dynamically create configuration sections on the fly to do translations to just use the libraries.
author: MCKRUZ

comments.body: @MCKRUZ  MSALConfiguration in optional.  But what you want is a way to set those programmatically instead of via config?

Correct.  It's not only in the MSALConfiguration though it's all over the Agent framework.  For example I had to create my own version of the ConfigurationConnections class in order to make it so I didn't have to setup my appsettings.json in a certain manner.  That class takes in a IConfiguration object which directly pulls from the appsettings.  I try whenever possible to not recreate code that Microsoft has already built since then I have to watch for any changes you guys make and then make the appropriate changes on my side.  It would just make life easier if it were more robust to handle configuration outside of appsettings.json.
@MCKRUZ How did you handle IConnections?  Though that is why that is an interface, and different implementations could be created.

@MCKRUZ It would be interesting to see some examples.  It would be more accurate to say it is currently IConfiguration based, which may be things other than appsettings.  A programmatic way seems reasonable for many cases, and as we move on from "preview" status we'd like to support more flexible means.

So I ended up creating my own version of the IConnections class.  In my project I have a POCO object called AppConfig that handles our rather large config.  So to circumvent all of the places where you guys utilized IConfiguration, I simply created a helper class that loads the configs into memory and spits out a IConfigurationSection object whenever I need it.

@MCKRUZ This is still on my radar.  Not ignoring this.  Most of the newer stuff allows for code-first config instead of just IConfiguration.  Just haven't fit it into the schedule yet to make that work for the initial implementation of some things.  Namely MsalAuth and Connections.

No worries tracy, I know you guys are slammed.  I have a work around for now.  I did see you added AgentApplicationOptions, I'm digging into that functionality now.  Cheers mate.  Don't stress, you guys are killing it.
